thread:
emma: Hey team — we're seeing our client SDK (EventSource) drop the SSE stream right before the final JSON payload. No finish_reason, connection just closes. This only started after we switched to the hosted endpoint and it's intermittent (~1-2% of calls, more on longer responses).

emma: Quick repro: Chrome EventSource to /v1/responses with streaming, we get a series of data: chunks, then an immediate close. The last chunk is a partial JSON fragment, e.g. `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}},` and then nothing. No `data: [DONE]` and no `finish_reason`.

emma: Example headers we see in client logs: `x-rw-req-id: req_abc123`, `x-forwarded-for`, `user-agent: our-app/1.2.3`.

emma: I tried enabling SDK auto-reconnect and it reopens and sometimes gets a duplicate tail token (duplicate content).

maria: Thanks — sorry about the hit. Can you confirm whether you're using the JS SDK or raw EventSource? Also, any proxy / CDN in front of you (corporate proxy, Cloudflare, Fastly)?

emma: We're on raw EventSource in the browser (no SDK wrapper). Traffic goes through our corporate gateway -> Fastly -> Redwood hosted. We can reproduce locally if we route straight through Fastly.

kevin: Noted. Does the network tab show a 200 then the socket close, or a non-2xx at the end? Any final bytes on the wire?

emma: Network tab shows 200 and then socket closed, no trailing bytes. I've attached a hex dump of the last 256 bytes from the capture: `...7b 22 63 68 6f 69 63 65 73 22 3a 5b 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 7b 22 63 6f 6e 74 65 6e 74 22 3a 22 2e 2e 2e` — that's `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...` and then FIN.

maria: OK can you paste the exact request-id `x-rw-req-id` and the time (timezone) of the failed call? We'll look in our edge logs.

emma: req_abc123 at 2026-03-15T14:02:11Z. One more datapoint: when it happens the account dashboard shows a short spike in usage and a quick throttle event in our billing UI for the same second (we have guardrails set).

kevin: Interesting — two hypotheses: (A) an upstream throttle/credit-limit enforcement is tearing the connection before the final event is emitted, or (B) Fastly/edge is sending a RST/FIN due to idle or connection pooling close. Both could produce a silent close.

kevin: To help repro locally, try this curl pipeline that mimics EventSource subscribe and prints bytes as they arrive:

kevin: ```
kevin: curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \nkevin:   -H "x-rw-req-id: req_abc123" \nkevin:   "https://api.redwood.com/v1/responses?stream=true" | hexdump -C -v | tail -n 40
kevin: ```

kevin: If you can reproduce with that and capture the last bytes, that helps us differentiate. Also confirm SDK version if you try the JS SDK — v0.10.0 had an auto-reconnect change that duplicates the last token in some edge cases.
\
emma: Ran curl, same silent close and same partial fragment. Pasted output to the thread.

arnav: I'm picking this up. I'll grep the Fastly edge logs for `req_abc123` and check backend response codes. If the billing guardrails triggered, the backend might return a 402/429 then the proxy could cut the stream mid-event.

arnav: Quick check: can you confirm whether the account has a hard cap or a soft alert? Soft alerts usually let the request finish, hard caps may terminate.
\
emma: We have a soft alert, not a hard cap. But the UI showed an immediate throttle spike for that second — could be our guardrail process misclassifying.

deploy-bot: deploy: ingest-edge-logs -> running search for req_abc123 on all edge nodes (this may take ~45s).

arnav: Found the edge trace for req_abc123. Backend responded 200, but the edge logged a `backend_reset` at the TCP layer 0.8s after the last token. No 4xx logged from backend. I also see repeated `FIN` from client-side connection reuse.

arnav: That pattern suggests the upstream (our side) didn't send the final event before the edge connection was closed. Two actionable next steps: (1) Support: ask customer to retry with `?retry_mode=dup-safe` to avoid duplicate tail tokens for now. (2) Infra: we'll instrument the response path to ensure final flush happens before connection termination and add a short keep-alive heartbeat frame if streaming > 2s.

maria: Emma — for the immediate workaround, can you try adding a client-side small timeout to wait 1s after connection close and then request the final state via non-streaming endpoint to recover the final JSON? That avoids duplicates.

emma: Will try and report back. Thanks.

arnav: I'm going to escalate to runtime team to adjust flush ordering and to add a guard in the edge that treats backend `200 + EOF` differently from `RST` so we can report clearer failure metadata. I'll update here after the patch. ETA 48h.

maria: Thanks everyone — assigning follow-up to arnav and kevin. Emma, we'll keep this thread updated and let you know when the patch is live. :thumbsup:
